item.title: Nathan Lyon, Marnus Labuschagne dropped! Pat Cummins continues as captain as Australia announce squad for New Zealand series
item.description: Jack Clayton and Corey Rocchiccioli have received their first-ever Test call-ups after being included in Australia's 13-member squad for the upcoming four-match series against New Zealand. The selection, however, comes with a notable omission, with veteran off-spinner Nathan Lyon left out of the Pat Cummins-led group. Clayton, a Queensland batter, has earned his place following an impressive run of performances in the Sheffield Shield. Western Australia off-spinner Rocchiccioli has also been rewarded for his consistent returns in domestic cricket and for Australia A. Australia squad: Pat Cummins (c), Scott Boland, Alex Carey, Jack Clayton, Cameron Green, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Michael Neser, Matthew Renshaw, Corey Rocchiccioli, Steve Smith, Mitchell Starc. One additional player will be named following the sixth round of the Sheffield Shield. The 27-year-old Clayton, a left-handed batter, has accumulated 2,732 runs in first-class cricket at an average of 40.17. His record includes seven centuries and 16 half-centuries. He has been particularly prolific in the ongoing Sheffield Shield campaign, scoring 449 runs from nine innings at an average of 74.83, including a century and four fifties. Rocchiccioli, meanwhile, has claimed 18 wickets in the Sheffield Shield this season at an average of 33.88. The 29-year-old has an overall tally of 205 wickets from 59 first-class appearances, with six five-wicket hauls to his name. There are several other changes to Australia's squad that featured in the third Test against South Africa. Marnus Labuschagne, Beau Webster, Cooper Connolly and Matthew Kuhnemann have all been left out, while Nic Maddinson and Sam Harper, who were released ahead of that Test, have not been recalled. Labuschagne endured a disappointing outing in South Africa, finishing the series with 131 runs from six innings at an average of 21.83. His highest score was 39. Lyon, who played two Tests, picked up six wickets at 43.66, with his best figures being 2 for 58. Webster managed 64 runs across four innings in the first two Tests against South Africa, while Connolly, who was part of the playing XI for the series-deciding Cape Town Test, scored 29 runs in two innings and picked up one wicket. However, Lyon's absence stands out as the most significant selection call. Australia's chair of selectors George Bailey admitted that leaving out the experienced off-spinner was a tough decision but stressed that he remained an important part of the team's plans. "Nathan has not quite had the impact we would like with the ball in recent matches," George Bailey, Australia's chair of selectors said. "We also know he has an extraordinary record and his experience, knowledge and skill can still be valuable to the program we have moving forward." The four-Test series against New Zealand begins on December 9, with Perth hosting the opening encounter. The teams will then travel to Adelaide, Melbourne and Sydney for the remaining three matches. item.description: MADISON, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 27: Colton Joseph #1 of the Wisconsin Badgers scores on a 7 yard touchdown run in the second quarter against the Minnesota Golden Gophers at Camp Randall Stadium on November 27, 2026 in Madison, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers were in dire need of a rivalry win, and they got that on Friday night, beating the Minnesota Gophers 28-5 to reclaim the Axe for the first time in three years. Wisconsin was completely dominant on both sides, putting together another complete win after their 42-10 beatdown of the Purdue Boilermakers last weekend. As a result, they got their first eight-win season under Luke Fickell, putting a bow on an up-and-down season with a much-needed win. Here are three quick takeaways from the Badgers 28-5 win over Minnesota on Friday. Dominance in the trenches As I said pregame, I thought the Badgers would win because they were able to win the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball. That’s exactly what happened as Wisconsin out-gained Minnesota 482-115. The Badgers averaged 5.2 yards per carry, with Colton Joseph eclipsing 100 rushing yards for the second straight game. Defensively, the Badgers held star running back Darius Taylor to just 14 rushing yards, as the Gophers averaged just 0.9 yards per carry. Wisconsin also consistently got pressure on the quarterback, disrupting the Gophers passing attack, leading to them scoring just three offensive points. It felt like this game would come down to trench play. And Wisconsin was the clear winner there. Third downs Wisconsin did a great job offensively getting itself in third-and-manageable scenarios, and they ended up converting 9 of 16 third downs. The Badgers averaged just a 5.8-yard-to-go distance, which allowed them to keep run options open. On the flip side, the Badgers consistently kept Minnesota in third-and-long, with the Gophers averaging 9.7 yards to go. They only converted 2 of 11 third downs, going three-and-out six times. Wisconsin also had some huge third-down plays. Their first touchdown came on a 3rd & 13, with Colton Joseph connecting with Tyrell Henry on a corner route for a 27-yard score. The Badgers also had a big catch-and-run from Colton Joseph on their long drive in the second quarter on 3rd & 5, going for 34 yards. Wisconsin would eventually score a touchdown on the drive. Then, in the fourth quarter, Eugene Hilton took an end around for 42 yards on 3rd & 4, getting the Badgers in the red zone. item.description: (Photo by Pim Waslander/Soccrates/Getty Images) | Getty Images Falk says there was no gentleman’s agreement (Sport Bild’s Christian Falk) Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala have been in a spat all week, but the battle seems to have subsided as both parties have agreed to take this fight off the streets. One of the more intriguing aspects of the story was whether there was a “gentlemen’s agreement” in place for Musiala to take a pay cut if his health did not improve. That always seems like a longshot, but there were some other interesting tidbits in the report: ❌It is NOT TRUE: Bayern had a gentlemen’s agreement (from the summer) with Jamal Musiala’s side that they could alter the contract. It’s true that there was a meeting at Uli Hoeneß’s residen ce in Tegernsee. I’ve been there a few times myself – quite often, I can say! I know a meeting took place, bu t there was absolutely no agreement with regard to what would or wouldn’t happen with the contract. They made a strategy, at this point, in terms of what would happen if this topic became public and how they could handle the situation with the medication. It was all about how Bayern could help Musiala in these special circumstances. Of course, ev eryone is more than aware of the fact that when two people are talking, sometimes not everyone hears the same thing. So, perhaps there was a little wish from the Bayern side that there could be something implemented so that there could be a later discussion about the financial side of things. But no, this just wasn’t a topic . There were some rumblings earlier in the week about the “gentlemen’s agreement” being nonsense, but that was only part of what interested me. The bold part struck me as a little curious. It is normal for journos to meet personalities for interviews on occasion, but given how much inside info that Sp ort Bild has gotten over the years, it — at least — made me pause for a second with my #TinFoilHatTheory that Thomas Müller was the m ole. item.description: Peoria, Ariz. - February 15: Freddy Fermin #54 and Luis Campusano #12 of the San Diego Padres look on during spring training workouts at the Peoria Sports Complex on Sunday, Feb. 15, 2026 in Peoria, Ariz.(Photo by Meg McLaughlin / The San Diego Union-Tribune via Getty Images) MLB Trade Rumors | Mark Polishuk : Ever since the trade deadline, the Yankees have made it very clear that they have wanted to add to their catching contingent, looking for a right-handed bat to go alongside the lefty-swinging Austin Wells. With San Diego looking to clear a path to playing time for top prospect Ethan Salas, two names that the Yankees have been looking into are Luis Campusano and Freddy Fermin. While both are right-handed hitters, their profiles are remarkably different: Fermin would give the Yankees one of the best defensive tandems in the game, and Campusano would provide some power behind the dish the team has desperately needed in recent years. item.title: ‘Rodgers was right’: Fans react after hearing what Mike McCarthy said after Steelers’ 27-5 win vs Broncos
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images Mike McCarthy was a happy man after the Pittsburgh Steelers beat the Denver Broncos 27-5. The head coach was at the centre of controversy all week following a few accusations from Aaron Rodgers before he was released from the organisation. The win on Friday was much-needed as a result, but what McCarthy said after the game has caught a few fans’ attention. Fans react after Mike McCarthy admits he hasn’t spent enough time with Steelers’ defence Rodgers clashed with McCarthy for a lot of reasons, one of which was because the latter apparently refused to be more involved with the defence and interact more with that side of the ball. However, after the dominant win against the Broncos, the Steelers head coach admitted that he hadn’t been spending enough time with the defence. “I have not spent enough time with the defence. That is something that, as far as job responsibility and job description, these things will be looked at in the off-season,” he said. That has given rise to mixed reactions from the fans, with some claiming that they respect McCarthy for taking responsibility, while others sided with Rodgers by claiming that he was right all along. One fan tweeted: “Everything Rodgers said was true. It straightened up McCarthy, and look at the difference. Rodgers lost his job but probably saved McCarthy.” Another wrote: “Rodgers was right again.” “I respect it. Instead of blaming, he holds himself accountable, which holds my highest respect,” said another. Another fan reacted by saying: “Kinda pathetic that a head coach needs to be called out to get a wake-up call in order for him to spend time with the defence.” “So he’s admitting that his insubordination toward Rodgers was correct, but Aaron was punished,” posted another. “He keeps admitting to the things Aaron Rodgers said. So what did they cut him for exactly?” questioned another. Whatever McCarthy did since Rodgers’ accusations seems to have worked, as the Steelers were terrific against the Broncos in their first game without him. Just two weeks ago, Pittsburgh conceded 38 points against the Cincinnati Bengals. To go from that to conceding just five on Friday shows massive improvement – it was arguably their sharpest, most disruptive defensive performance of the 2026 season. Up next for the Steelers is a game against the Houston Texans. It remains to be seen if they can replicate this performance then.

After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
